items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider the horizontal hyperbola whose equation is

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{10} - \dfrac{y^2}{25} = 1,]

Content:
and whose graph is shown below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/dca18da1cd45e82fb074958c2a7a70ad]

Content:
The two dotted lines are the asymptotes of the hyperbola. As [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] get larger in absolute value, the hyperbola gets closer and closer to the asymptotes, but they never intersect. On the other hand, the asymptotes intersect each other at the center of the hyperbola.

Content:
Recall that the equation of general horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is given by

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1.]

Content:
The equations of the asymptotes of a general horizontal hyperbola are

Content:
[MATH: y = \pm \dfrac{b}{a}x.]

Content:
From the equation of the hyperbola shown in the diagram above, we have that [MATH: a = \sqrt {10}] and [MATH: b = \sqrt{25} = 5.] Therefore, the equations of asymptotes are
[MATH: y = ± (5)/(sqrt(10))x.]

Content:
Finally, if we rationalize the denominator in the above equation, we get

Content:
[MATH: y = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{2}x.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

[MATH: \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2}=1.]

For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

[MATH: y=\pm \dfrac{b}{a}x.]

In our case, we have

[MATH: a=\sqrt{36} = 6, \qquad b=\sqrt9 =3.]

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

[MATH: y|= ± (3)/(6)x; = ± (1)/(2)x.]

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola [MATH: 25 x ^ 2 - 9 y ^ 2 = 225].

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is [MATH: \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2}=1.] For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are [MATH: y=\pm \dfrac{b}{a}x.]

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: 225] and then simplify, as follows: [MATH: 25x^{2} − 9y^{2}|= 225; (25x^{2})/(225) − (9y^{2})/(225)|= (225)/(225); (x^{2})/(9) − (y^{2})/(25)|= 1]

So, we have [MATH: a=\sqrt 9 = 3,] and [MATH: b=\sqrt{25} = 5.]

Therefore, the asymptotes are [MATH: y=\pm \dfrac{5}{3}x.]
